nations.name: Fort Sill Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Apache and Fletcher, Oklahoma; reservation land in New Mexico, United States

facts.text: The Fort Sill Apache Tribe comprises descendants of Chiricahua and Warm Springs Apaches displaced from the Southwest and northern Mexico.
facts.evidence: descendants of the Chiricahua and Warm Springs Apaches

facts.text: In 1894, Chiricahua Apache prisoners were moved to Oklahoma after imprisonment and exile in Florida and Alabama.
Apache families who remained at Fort Sill were released in 1914 and resettled on scattered farmland near Apache and Fletcher, Oklahoma.
The Tribe reports that its New Mexico reservation proclamation was issued in November 2011, following its efforts to regain a land base in its homeland.
facts.evidence: this was issued in November of 2011

facts.text: The General Council, made up of adult tribal members, elects the Business Committee and approves the tribal operations budget.
facts.evidence: General Council votes to approve the tribal operations budget
